title: Sell Mineral Rights in Edgerton, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Edgerton, WY | Salt Creek
metaDescription: Own minerals near Edgerton, WY on the old Salt Creek field? Get a fair cash offer for your Natrona County royalty or mineral interest, no obligation.
heroLead: Edgerton sits on the edge of the Salt Creek field, one of the oldest producing oil fields in the Rocky Mountains. That history shows up in the deed room.
intro: Salt Creek has been producing since before Wyoming had paved highways. Wells drilled in the 1910s and 1920s got re-drilled, unitized, and re-worked through half a dozen operator changes, and every one of those transactions left paper in the Natrona County Clerk's office. If you hold minerals under or near Edgerton, chances are your interest came down through a family that homesteaded here two or three generations ago and never sold, just kept cashing whatever check showed up.

sections.heading: What's actually producing around Edgerton
paragraphs: The shallow Salt Creek sands (Wall Creek, Second Wall Creek, Frontier) are mostly stripper production now, low volume, long decline curves, operated by smaller independents who bought the legacy leases off the majors decades back. Newer horizontal work in the deeper Niobrara and Turner has moved through parts of Natrona County too, and where those units overlap old Salt Creek acreage you can end up with two different operators sending two different statements for the same section.

sections.heading: Why the ownership is usually split six ways
paragraphs: Original Salt Creek-era mineral grants got willed, divorced, and probated across a century. A quarter section that started with one owner in 1918 might be held by fourteen heirs today, each with a sliver of a decimal interest. Small interests like that get expensive for operators to track and easy for owners to lose interest in, which is exactly when people start asking what the acreage is worth.

sections.heading: Reading your Edgerton royalty check
paragraphs: Stripper wells decline slow but steady, a few percent a year, so your check five years from now will likely be smaller than it is today even with no drop in price. Buyers price that decline into an offer. Bring your most recent two or three check stubs and your division order when you want a real number instead of a guess.

faqs.question: Is my Edgerton interest still producing?
faqs.answer: Most legacy Salt Creek-area interests are still on some kind of stripper production, even at low volume. Pull your last check stub or call the county clerk to confirm the well status before you assume it's dry.

faqs.question: What county records do I need?
faqs.answer: Natrona County Clerk's office in Casper holds the deed and probate records. If your interest passed through an estate, bring the probate case number along with your deed.

faqs.question: Does age of the field lower the value?
faqs.answer: It affects it, it doesn't kill it. Older stripper production is valued on current volume and decline, not on when the field was discovered. Newer horizontal activity nearby can also lift interest even on old legacy tracts.
